newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-RONALDO CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY WITH DOUBLE STRIKE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO CELEBRATES BIRTHDAY WITH DOUBLE STRIKE.

text.p: Brazilian striker Ronaldo celebrated his 20th birthday with two goals in Barcelona's rain-soaked 3-2 victory over Real Sociedad on Sunday.
With 10 points from four games, Barcelona are second on goal difference to surprise league leaders Real Betis, 2-0 winners at Celta Vigo.
One point back are Oviedo, and a further point behind them Deportivo Coruna and Real Madrid -- who struggled to an unconvincing 1-0 victory over Rayo Vallecano.
Ronaldo opened his account in the second minute after latching on to a ball from Portuguese midfielder Luis Figo and hit the bar with a header minutes afterwards.
The game was suspended for nearly half an hour at the break because of an intense rain-storm, which at one stage caused a power cut.

When play resumed it was Real Sociedad who adapted better to the conditions, equalising through Alberto Albistegi. But Barcelona went ahead again through Juan Pizzi and Ronaldo before Real's Darko Kovacevic scored a consolation last-minute penalty.

Another Brazilian, Deportivo Coruna's Rivaldo, scored twice in his side's 4-0 trouncing of Hercules, while teenager Raul Gonzalez once again saved Real Madrid with the solitary goal in their home win over struggling neighbours Rayo Vallecano.
Watching the game was Diego Maradona, who is in Spain for medical treatment and has said he will shortly announce his decision whether to retire from soccer.

Real Betis went to Celta Vigo as leaders for the first time in a decade, and after defending well in the first half, came out to score through Alexis Trujillo and again just before the final whistle through Tomas Olias.

In Saturday's games reigning champions Atletico Madrid woke up after two consecutive defeats to brush aside Logrones 3-0, while Romario scored on his return to the Valencia line-up in their 2-1 victory over Tenerife.
But the Brazilian striker will not be able to play in Valencia's crucial UEFA Cup second leg tie at Bayern Munich because of a knee injury picked up in the game.
Another UEFA Cup side, Espanyol, came back from 2-0 down to earn a point at Athletic Bilbao, while Racing Santander crashed 3-0 at Valladolid.
